known_facts_book1: The wheezing, asthmatic innkeeper of the Hôtel du Commerce in Tôtes, a former horse-dealer; inherited the name Follenvie from his father.
Is the sole go-between the Prussian officer allows to speak to him about the travelers' civil affairs.
Twice relays the officer's question to Boule de Suif, asking whether she has changed her mind.
Refuses to be woken before ten in the morning because of his asthma, except in case of fire.
Sits up late playing cards with the male travelers, ignoring their attempts to draw him out about the officer, only ever repeating 'Au jeu, messieurs, au jeu.'
Sells Loiseau six casks of Bordeaux for after the Prussians have left.
Confirms to the count, in a whispered exchange, that Boule de Suif has finally given in to the officer.

known_relations_book1.Mme Follenvie: His wife; tells her to be quiet at dinner when she complains too loudly about the Prussians.
known_relations_book1.l'officier prussien: The only person the officer permits to relay messages about the travelers.
known_relations_book1.Boule de Suif: Twice brings her the officer's demand and eventually confirms to the count that she has yielded.

not_in_this_book: M. Follenvie is a Prussian sympathizer

known_facts_book1: Wife of the innkeeper; talks constantly, unlike her wheezing husband, who can barely speak while eating.
Complains at length to the countess about the Prussians eating nothing but potatoes and pork and living off the country without working the land.
Has two sons in the French army, which is part of why the occupation costs her dearly.
Argues, to Cornudet's approval, that killing people is wicked even when it is Prussians, English or Poles who die, unless done in self-defense.
Always rises with the sun ('du matin'), unlike her husband who stays up with his card-playing guests ('du soir').

known_relations_book1.M. Follenvie: Her husband; he tells her to hush when she speaks too freely at dinner.
known_relations_book1.la comtesse de Bréville: Addresses most of her complaints about the Prussians to her, flattered to be talking with a lady of quality.
